newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Short position rolled forward in Railtrack.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Short position rolled forward in Railtrack.

text.p: A number of UK stock options were active on Wednesday as the stock market raced up initially only to backtrack in a volatile session, dealers said.
A short call position was rolled forward in railway network operator Railtrack and in electricals group GEC the biggest deal was bull spread.

In Railtrack the main deal was to buy back 1,000 June 580 calls at 64p -- to close an existing position -- and then to sell 1,000 September 580 calls at 77p. With the stock price closing up 3p to 644-1/2p, the short calls have 12-1/2p time value and so carry little risk of assignment at present.
In general, if Railtrack shares drop the call premiums will also fall and the short position can then be closed at a profit.
In GEC, a bull spread was established by buying 500 August 330 calls at 17p and selling 500 August 360 calls at 5p making a net debit of 12p.
If GEC shares go above 360p at expiry, the maximum profit from the deal will be 18p. Below 330p the maximum loss will be 12p. GEC shares were down 2p to 333-1/2p.
Elsewhere there was a buyer of 1,500 July 160 calls at 2-1/2p in British Steel and a crossed trade in electricity generator National Power.
The deal in National Power concerned 1,000 July 500 puts which were traded at 13p.
GEC shares closed down 2-1/2p to 333p while those of National Power were fell 2p to 503-1/2p.

Call buying was also predominant in food and drinks group Allied Domecq in which 500 July 460 calls were bought at 12p and in soft drinks and confectionery group Cadbury Schweppes where 500 August 280 calls were bought at 4-1/2p. Allied Domecq ended the day 6-1/2p weaker to 429-1/2p and Cadbury Schweppes slipped 4p to 522-1/2p.
